```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)


library("dplyr") # data cleaning and handling
library("modelsummary") # outputting results where needed
library(tidyr) 
library(broom)
library(purrr)
library(srvyr) # used for logit regressions with complex survey designs
library(svyVGAM) # used for PPO regressions with complex survey designs 
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)

# Load project configuration
source(here::here("R", "load_config.R"))
cfg <- load_config()

# Construct input file path
input_2024 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2024_1year
)

input_2019 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2019_1year
)

input_means <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$outout_file_ACS_1year_means
)

input_dis <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_ACS_1year_IncDis
)


## independent variables to be used in the regressions below.  This means you only
## need to update them here.

x_vector <- ("HHSize + ChildPresent + SeniorPresent + AGE + LF + SEX + ChildPresent*HHSize+AGE*LF") 

stopifnot(file.exists(input_2019))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_2024))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_means))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_dis))

```

## load the 2024 data and test which variables do or do not meet parallel lines assumption 
 
```{r}

ACS_1year_2024 <- read.csv(file.path(input_2024)) ## loads 2024 data

#restoring ordered factor nature to the ordered factor varriable
ACS_1year_2024$IncCat <- ordered(ACS_1year_2024$IncCat, levels = paste0("Inc", 1:14))

ACS_1year_means <-read.csv(file.path(input_means))

ACS_1year_dis <-read.csv(file.path(input_dis))

Weighted_IPUMS <-as_survey(ACS_1year_2024, id=CLUSTER,
                           weights=HHWT,
                           strata=STRATA,
                           nest=TRUE)

## Goal here is to test the Partial Proportional Odds Model (PPO).  This model allows you 
## to take advantage of the fact that you have ordinal data for variables which
## meet the parallel lines assumption, and let them vary randomly for the variables
## which do not meet that assumption. In order to test if we should use a PPO
## we would normally use a Brant Test.  That test effectively looks at if the coefficients 
## (B) are close enough in the separate logistic models to have parallel slopes
## after accounting for difference from sampling. However we have a complex survey
## design featuring stratification which does not line up with the random sampling
## assumption in the Brant test. This modification of the Brant test which uses
## R's survey package to introduce the sampling weights.  The blog post detailing it
## can be found here https://notstatschat.rbind.io/2023/02/09/checking-proportionality-of-odds/

# set our formula, this saves us from retyping it for all the individual logistic
# regressions and lets us test alternative specifications


formula <- as.formula(
  paste("IncCat ~", x_vector)
)

 
#setting up the ordered logit model with weights
m1 <-svyolr(formula, design = Weighted_IPUMS)

K<-length(m1$lev) # acquire levels of the ordered category Income_Cat
P<-length(m1$coef) # acquire # of coefficients which is 6 but we can change the model

#get influence function which allows covariance matrix to be computed
#this fist block defines the influence function
get_infl <-function(k,formula,design){
  y<-formula[[2]]
  formula[[2]]<-bquote(I(as.numeric(.(y))>.(k)))
  mk<-svyglm(formula, design, family= quasibinomial, influence=TRUE) #quasibinomial is the svglm package's logistic regression
  list(coef(mk), attr(mk, "influence"))
  }

#this second block calls it and get the covariance matrix
# lapply applied the function over each of our levels, running a binomial
# regression for each level of the function, except the last which is the omitted category
fits<-lapply(1:(K-1), function(k) get_infl(k, formula, Weighted_IPUMS))
infs<-do.call(cbind,lapply(fits,"[[",2))
combined_V<- vcov(svytotal(infs/weights(Weighted_IPUMS), Weighted_IPUMS))

# now we extract the coefficients we care about to make the comparison
conditional_V<- lapply(1:P, 
                       function(p) 1/diag(solve(combined_V[c(p+1+(0:(K-2))*(P+1)), c(p+1+(0:(K-2))*(P+1))])))
coefs<-lapply(fits,"[[",1)


## An initial visual test, if the point estimates on the coefficients are all within
## one anther's error bars we are probably ok to use the ordinal model for that
## coefficient, otherwise that var fails the parallel lines assumption
## we can then make a modified formula and run it through the Brant test located
## in the next code block

res <- data.frame(
  variable = rep(names(coefs[[1]])[-1], each = K - 1),
  cutpoint = rep(names(m1$zeta), P),
  estimate = as.vector(do.call(rbind, coefs)[,-1]),
  se = sqrt(do.call(c, conditional_V))
)

res$cutpoint <- factor(
  res$cutpoint,
  levels = rev(names(m1$zeta)),
  ordered = TRUE
)

res$lower <- res$estimate - 1.96 * res$se
res$upper <- res$estimate + 1.96 * res$se

p<-ggplot(res,aes(y=cutpoint,col=cutpoint))+
  geom_point(aes(x=estimate))+
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin=lower,xmax=upper))+
  facet_wrap(~variable,scales="free")+
  theme(legend.position="none")+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=z),linetype="dotted",
             data.frame(z=m1$coef,variable=names(coefs[[1]])[-1]))
print(p)


```

## modified brant test
```{r}

## here is then the modified Brant test which looks at how far away the unconstrained betas are from one another
## specifically testing if B_{kp}=T_kB_p where T_k is  

D<-diag(P)
for(k in 2:(K-1)){
  D<-rbind(D,diag(P))
}
D<-cbind(D,matrix(0,nrow=(P)*(K-1),ncol=(K-2)))
for (k in 1:(K-2)){
  D[(P-1)*k+(1:(P)),P+k]<-coefs[[k+1]][-1]
}       

B<-do.call(c,lapply(coefs, "[",-1))
VarB<-(combined_V[-(1+(0:(K-2))*(P+1)),-(1+(0:(K-2))*(P+1))])
VarBinv<-solve(VarB)
deltahat<- solve(t(D)%*%VarBinv%*%D, t(D)%*%VarBinv%*%B)
VarDelta<-solve(t(D)%*%VarBinv%*%D)

i<-P+(1:(K-2))
brantTest<-deltahat[i]%*%solve(VarDelta[i,i])%*%deltahat[i]
brantTest  #this is the test statistic 

#Brant test is a chi squared test with K-2 degrees of freedom so we run it though
# the pchisq command to get a P value
# Null is that parallel lines assumption holds, 
pchisq(brantTest,df=(K-2),lower.tail=FALSE)





```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
